svg.title: Delegated action (v1.3): an external orchestrator commands a registered action under a grant chain; the gate verifies the chain, the registry names the handler, which is a deterministic process (B) or an agent (A)

g.text: Delegated action (v1.3): an external orchestrator commands a registered action under a grant chain; the gate verifies the chain, the registry names the handler, which is a deterministic process (B) or an agent (A)
(other owner's user, key signed by G2)
(other owner's user, key signed by G2)
G1: owner root -> external owner key K_alexis:
G2: K_alexis -> their orchestrator key: subset of G1
registry: namespace github-runner.* -> handler (A or B), schema
target host:mini/runners/x, grant_refs [G2, G1], expiry, nonce}
canonical bytes; key_id pinned? signature ok?
chain G2 -> G1 -> our root: each link signed by its issuer,
subject == next issuer, actions/targets narrow, expiries nested;
revocation snapshot; freshness; replay; target binding
decision guard: request fits the grants and the schema;
enqueue(action item, authoritative, verification_ref) for admin_orch
stdin: validated command <id>, fetch from mailbox
optional re-verification; judgement (safe to restart now?)
execute through the helper or its own narrow sudo rule
re-verify the chain itself (never trusts the bridge alone)
one registered operation: restart runner x; audit line
receipt applied | refused{reason}, signed by the helper's identity
receipt visible to the external orchestrator
No free text in the authority layer: the action is a registered
name with a schema; the target is concrete; wildcards exist only
in grants. The requester never judges its own request.
